research_question: Can a real model result settled in PALACE Information Space outlive its producer Execution State and OS process, then be restored as a verified input in a genuinely new Execution State/process for incremental continuation without re-generating the completed task?
primary_claim: A semantically sufficient, dependency-complete, valid settled U1 result can be detached from the old execution context and reused through IS by a new native production task execution for U2.
not_in_scope: database-wide anti-rollback or remote/hardware trust root work
changes to carrier_loop / execute_demand recompute semantics
KV optimization or performance benchmarking as the primary goal
generic chat/engine paths not executing task items
changing old experiment evidence or model-weight copying

phases.goal: Create before-change workspace and historical-artifact snapshots; map actual native call graph and KV/context ownership.
Make a native Swift driver own U1 and U2 process/ExecutionState lifecycle; ordinary continueTask performs the IS admission itself.
requirements: U1 actual model generation and signed settlement
per-call counters at real call sites

conditions.expected: U1 settles runtime nonce A; U1 process exits; fresh U2 restores A from IS through ordinary continueTask and generates exactly once.
Independent nonce B and complete settlement lineage; same byte-identical nonce-free U2 base template; fresh U2 output follows B, not A.
ordinary continueTask refuses before text/seed tokenization and generation; no item/source fallback.
no nonce/prefix leakage into base template, cold seed, U2 state, argv, env, disallowed files/logs or the other world.

conclusion_objects.C2: The exact value consumed by U2 comes from the verified U1 IS settlement, with no old prompt/prefix/side-channel copy.
conclusion_objects.C3: Observe existing path behavior only; do not change recompute policy.
conclusion_objects.C4: Use existing E-round signature/provenance validation as prerequisite; do not expand into store-wide anti-rollback. Signature does not prove semantic correctness.
